survival_detail: PacWest did not fail, was not seized and was not acquired in May 3-6 2023 or the following week. No FDIC action. It funded outflows from on-balance-sheet liquidity and pledged more collateral to the Fed discount window on May 10 (borrowing capacity, not a reported emergency bailout). Later: merger with Banc of California announced 2023-07-25 (all-stock, 0.6569 BANC share per PACW share, $400m Warburg Pincus/Centerbridge equity); closed Nov 30 2023.

outflow_figures.window: Week ended Fri May 5 2023 (Mon May 1 - Fri May 5)
outflow_figures.source: PacWest SEC filing disclosed May 10-11 2023 (reported by CNBC, Reuters, Motley Fool, The Bank Slate as an 8-K/10-Q item): deposits 'declined approximately 9.5%', with a majority on May 4 and 5 after May 3 afternoon news reports. Dollar amount is my arithmetic: 9.5% x ~$28bn (8-K exhibit dated 2023-05-03: 'total deposits totaling $28 billion as of May 2, 2023'). Reuters-based secondary coverage cited ~$1.5bn, which does not reconcile with 9.5% of $28bn and is treated as unreliable. Exact filing form (8-K vs 10-Q) conflicted across sources; I could not open the filing text itself.

outflow_figures.window: May 4-5 2023 (two days after May 3 reports) - UNVERIFIED
outflow_figures.source: A search summary attributed a ~$1.7bn two-day decline after the May 3 board meeting to a securities filing (likely the Banc of California merger proxy 'Background of the Merger'); I could not confirm it in primary text. It is consistent with 'majority of 9.5%' (1.7/2.7 = ~64%).

outflow_figures.window: Q1-end to Q2-end context: Mar 31 to Jun 30 2023
outflow_figures.source: PacWest Q2 2023 10-Q: total deposits fell $6.0bn (17.8%) to $27.9bn at Jun 30; noninterest-bearing down $5.2bn. Also base: $28.2bn deposits at Mar 31 (Bloomberg). Insured share 75% on May 2.

best_estimate_window.derivation: Window is Wed May 3 18:00 PT to Sat May 6 18:00 PT, i.e. effectively Thu May 4 and Fri May 5 (Sat has no business-day flows; Wed afternoon outflows before 18:00 are excluded but the news broke after Wed's market close/afternoon). The company said the majority of the 9.5% weekly decline came on May 4 and 5, and its own May 3 statement said flows were not out-of-the-ordinary through May 2/3, so Mon-Wed were roughly flat. Hence the window captures the bulk of the 9.5% (~$2.7bn on ~$28bn). Point estimate 7% (~$1.9-2.0bn) assumes ~70-75% of the week fell on May 4-5 and about 6% (~$1.7bn, unverified proxy figure) at the low end; the upper bound is the whole weekly 9.5% (~$2.7bn) if Mon-Wed was flat/slightly positive. Low 5.5% allows a larger Mon-Wed share or an intraday May 3 share.

leading_segments: Not disclosed in available sources. No filing or news found that breaks the May 4-5 outflows down by segment or geography. Context only: uninsured deposits were ~25% of deposits ($5.2bn on May 10; insured 75% on May 2); PacWest has a large venture/technology banking and California business franchise; Q2 outflows were concentrated in noninterest-bearing (business operating) accounts ($5.2bn of the $6.0bn Q1-end to Q2-end drop) - suggests commercial/uninsured clients led, but this is inference, not reported for the May window.
peak_dates: Thu May 4 and Fri May 5 2023 (company: majority of the week's 9.5% decline occurred on those days, following afternoon May 3 Bloomberg report that PacWest was exploring strategic options incl. sale/capital raise). Stock fell to record lows May 4; rebounded Mon May 8 after dividend cut announcement. Disclosure on Thu May 11 caused a second stock plunge (-23%/-28% intraday) but that was disclosure of the prior week's outflows, not a new run peak.

actions_in_window.action: 8-K exhibit (dated May 3): said no out-of-the-ordinary deposit flows, deposits $28bn as of May 2, 75% insured, liquidity 188% of uninsured deposits, repaid $1bn borrowings, board continuously reviewing strategic options.
Bloomberg/press reported PacWest weighing strategic options incl. sale; stock sold off sharply; PacWest confirmed it reviews options and said no cause for alarm.

Cut quarterly common dividend from $0.25 to $0.01 per share to accelerate capital build toward CET1 10%+; CEO Paul Taylor quoted. Stock jumped ~39% premarket Mon May 8 (note: some outlets also cite a large Friday rebound).
Pledged additional $5.1bn loans to the FRB, adding ~$3.9bn discount window capacity; immediately available liquidity $15.0bn vs uninsured deposits $5.2bn (288%).
Disclosed 9.5% weekly deposit decline; stock fell ~20-28% intraday. Earlier (pre-window) Q1 10-Q booked $1.38bn goodwill impairment.

caveats: Could not open the May 11 primary filing text; 9.5% and 'majority on May 4-5' are from multiple consistent secondary reports quoting it.
Dollar amounts are derived from the ~$28bn base.
Reuters-reported $1.5bn figure and $1.7bn two-day figure conflict/unverified.
